units.title: Rapor
units.description: Verileri ve bulguları başlıklı, önerili bir rapor hâlinde yaz
units.guide:
## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- Bir rapordaki rakamları, bulguları ve önerileri bulabilirsin.
- Toplantıda ve sunumda geçen artış, düşüş ve yüzdeleri dinleyerek anlayabilirsin.
- Bir çalışmanın sonuçlarını bir dakikada sözlü olarak özetleyebilirsin.
- Veri ve bulguları başlıklı, önerili 200 kelimelik bir rapor olarak yazabilirsin.

## Strateji
- Raporu okurken önce başlıklara bak: **Introduction, Findings, Recommendations**. Aradığın bilgi hangi başlığın altında?
- Rakam duyduğunda yönüne dikkat et: **rise / increase by** mı, **fall / drop by** mı? Karşılaştırmayı da yakala: **compared with**, **twice the figure**.
- Gölgeleme (shadowing): cümleyi dinle, hemen ardından aynı ritimle tekrarla. **per cent**, **on the whole** gibi kalıplar ağzına yerleşsin.
- Hikâyeyi önce metni görmeden dinle ve soruları cevapla. Sonra metni açıp kaçırdığın rakamları bul.
- Raporda her bulguyu bir rakamla destekle, önerileri numaralı yaz ve kişisel duygudan kaçın.

## Model metin
> Report: Small vans for city deliveries
>
> Introduction
> This report presents the results of a six-month study on delivery vans in Istanbul. Its aim is to decide whether small vans should replace some of our trucks.
>
> Method
> We tracked 200 deliveries in Kadıköy and Beşiktaş. Half were made with trucks and half with small vans.
>
> Findings
> The results were clear. Fuel use fell by 21 per cent, and the cost per delivery dropped from 90 to 74 lira. Customers were also more satisfied, as the vans could park closer to their doors. However, the vans were not suitable for heavy orders, and drivers needed about two weeks to learn the new routes.
>
> Limitations
> The study only covered two districts, so the results may be different in other parts of the city.
>
> Recommendations
> Based on these findings, we recommend the following:
> 1. Replace ten old trucks with small vans next year.
> 2. Test the vans in two more districts before making further changes.
> 3. Keep two trucks for heavy orders.
>
> Conclusion
> On the whole, the evidence suggests that small vans are cheaper and greener. A gradual change is the safest option.

Yapı: başlık, amaç (Introduction), yöntem, rakamlı bulgular, sınırlılıklar, numaralı öneriler ve tek cümlelik sonuç. Bulgularda **However**, sonuçta **On the whole** kullanılıyor; öneriler **we recommend** ile resmî kalıyor.

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ Costs fell with 8 per cent. ✅ Costs fell **by** 8 per cent. (Değişimin miktarı **by** ile verilir: rise by, drop by.)
- ❌ Aim of this report is to compare the branches. ✅ **The** aim of this report is to compare the branches. (Belirli bir şeyden söz ediyorsan **the**: the results, the study.)

Report: The Moda branch after three months
Prepared by Elif, with data from Kerem's ordering app

Introduction
This report looks at the first three months of our second café, which opened in Moda in March. Its aim is to compare the new branch with our first café and to suggest changes for the summer. The data comes from the till, from the ordering app and from a short survey that 240 customers completed.

Findings
Sales: The Moda branch served around 9,000 customers, roughly 70 per cent of the first café's number. However, the average bill was higher: 185 lira compared with 150 lira. In other words, people there come less often but spend more.
Busy times: What surprised us most was the timing. In the first café, the busiest hours are between eight and ten in the morning. In Moda, almost half of all orders arrive after four in the afternoon, mainly from students and people working on laptops.
The app: Around 35 per cent of orders in Moda were placed through the app, which is twice the figure for the first café. Customers who used it waited an average of four minutes, against nine minutes for those who ordered at the counter.
Survey: Most customers (82 per cent) rated the coffee as excellent. On the other hand, 41 per cent said the café was too noisy in the evenings, and many complained about the lack of power sockets.
Costs: Rent remains the biggest problem. It currently takes up 38 per cent of the branch's income, which is clearly too high in the long term.

Recommendations
1. Open one hour later in the morning and stay open until eleven at night from June to September.
2. Create a quiet area with extra sockets for people who want to work.
3. Offer a small discount to customers who order through the app, since this reduces queues.
4. Try to renegotiate the rent before the contract is renewed in January.

Conclusion
On the whole, the first three months have been a success. The branch has found its own customers, and they are rather different from those of our first café. If we adapt to them rather than copy the original, Moda could become profitable within a year.

nodes.title: Rapor için rakamlar
nodes.description: Müdür, Deniz'den konferanstaki verileri yönetim kurulu için bir rapora dönüştürmesini istiyor

steps.speaker: Müdür
steps.text: Deniz, everyone is still talking about your conference talk. Well done. Now I need something a little less exciting from you.
steps.translation: Deniz, herkes hâlâ konferanstaki konuşmanı konuşuyor. Tebrikler. Şimdi senden biraz daha az heyecan verici bir şey istiyorum.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Let me guess. A report?
steps.translation: Tahmin edeyim. Bir rapor mu?

steps.speaker: Müdür
steps.text: Exactly. The board meets on the fifteenth, and they want the van study in writing. No slides, no jokes, just the facts.
steps.translation: Aynen öyle. Yönetim kurulu ayın on beşinde toplanıyor ve kamyonet çalışmasını yazılı olarak istiyorlar. Slayt yok, şaka yok, sadece gerçekler.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: That's fine. Most of the data is already in my presentation. I'll just need to organise it properly.
steps.translation: Sorun değil. Verilerin çoğu zaten sunumumda var. Sadece onları düzgünce düzenlemem gerekecek.

steps.speaker: Müdür
steps.text: Good. So remind me of the key figures. How many deliveries did you track in the end?
steps.translation: Güzel. O zaman bana temel rakamları hatırlat. Sonunda kaç teslimatı takip ettiniz?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Two hundred over six months, all in Kadıköy and Beşiktaş. Half with the big trucks and half with the small vans.
steps.translation: Altı ayda iki yüz, hepsi Kadıköy ve Beşiktaş'ta. Yarısı büyük kamyonlarla, yarısı küçük kamyonetlerle.

steps.speaker: Müdür
steps.text: And the fuel saving was twenty per cent?
steps.translation: Yakıt tasarrufu da yüzde yirmi miydi?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Twenty-one, to be precise. But what the board will care about more is the cost per delivery. It fell from ninety lira to seventy-four.
steps.translation: Tam olarak yüzde yirmi bir. Ama yönetim kurulunun daha çok önemseyeceği şey teslimat başına maliyet. Doksan liradan yetmiş dörde düştü.

steps.prompt: Teslimat başına maliyet kaç liraya düştü?

steps.speaker: Müdür
steps.text: Now that's a number they'll remember. Were there any problems?
steps.translation: İşte akılda kalacak bir rakam. Hiç sorun çıktı mı?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: A few. The small vans can't carry heavy furniture, so we still needed two trucks for some orders. And the drivers took a while to learn the new routes.
steps.translation: Birkaç tane. Küçük kamyonetler ağır mobilya taşıyamıyor, bu yüzden bazı siparişler için yine iki kamyona ihtiyacımız oldu. Sürücülerin yeni rotaları öğrenmesi de biraz zaman aldı.

steps.speaker: Müdür
steps.text: Put that in. The board doesn't trust reports that sound too perfect.
steps.translation: Bunu da yaz. Yönetim kurulu fazla mükemmel görünen raporlara güvenmez.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Agreed. I was planning a section called Limitations anyway. It was the limitations that the audience asked about most at the conference.
steps.translation: Katılıyorum. Zaten Sınırlılıklar diye bir bölüm planlıyordum. Konferansta dinleyicilerin en çok sorduğu şey sınırlılıklardı.

steps.prompt: Müdür sorunların da rapora yazılmasını neden istiyor?
choices: Yönetim kurulu fazla mükemmel görünen raporlara güvenmediği için
Deniz sunumda sorunlardan hiç bahsetmediği için
steps.answer: Yönetim kurulu fazla mükemmel görünen raporlara güvenmediği için

steps.speaker: Müdür
steps.text: How long should it be? Last year somebody sent them forty pages, and nobody read past page three.
steps.translation: Ne uzunlukta olmalı? Geçen yıl biri onlara kırk sayfa göndermişti ve kimse üçüncü sayfadan öteye okumadı.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Four pages at most. A one-paragraph summary at the top, then the method, the findings, the limitations and my recommendations.
steps.translation: En fazla dört sayfa. En üstte bir paragraflık özet, sonra yöntem, bulgular, sınırlılıklar ve önerilerim.

steps.speaker: Müdür
steps.text: And what exactly are you going to recommend?
steps.translation: Peki tam olarak ne önereceksin?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Two things. First, we replace ten old trucks with small vans next year. Second, we test the vans in two more districts before we go any further.
steps.translation: İki şey. Birincisi, gelecek yıl on eski kamyonun yerine küçük kamyonet alalım. İkincisi, daha ileri gitmeden önce kamyonetleri iki ilçede daha deneyelim.

steps.prompt: Deniz gelecek yıl kaç eski kamyonun değiştirilmesini öneriyor?

steps.speaker: Müdür
steps.text: Why not replace all of them at once? It would save more money.
steps.translation: Neden hepsini birden değiştirmiyoruz? Daha çok para tasarruf ederiz.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: It would, but the study only covered two districts. If the results are different in Üsküdar, for example, we'd lose a lot of money very quickly.
steps.translation: Ederiz, ama çalışma sadece iki ilçeyi kapsadı. Örneğin Üsküdar'da sonuçlar farklı çıkarsa çok hızlı bir şekilde çok para kaybederiz.

steps.speaker: Müdür
steps.text: Fair enough. Careful, but not too careful. I like it.
steps.translation: Haklısın. Dikkatli ama aşırı dikkatli değil. Hoşuma gitti.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: One more thing. Could I include a chart that shows the monthly costs? It makes the trend much easier to see.
steps.translation: Bir şey daha. Aylık maliyetleri gösteren bir grafik ekleyebilir miyim? Eğilimi görmeyi çok kolaylaştırıyor.

steps.speaker: Müdür
steps.text: Of course. Just make sure it has a clear title. The chairman hates charts he can't understand.
steps.translation: Tabii. Sadece net bir başlığı olduğundan emin ol. Başkan anlayamadığı grafiklerden nefret eder.

steps.prompt: "Just make sure it has a clear title" cümlesindeki 'it' neyi anlatıyor?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Noted. I'll send you a first draft on Monday, so you've got time to comment before it goes to the board.
steps.translation: Not aldım. Pazartesi sana ilk taslağı gönderirim, böylece yönetim kuruluna gitmeden önce yorum yapmaya vaktin olur.

steps.speaker: Müdür
steps.text: Perfect. And Deniz? Write it in plain English. Nobody has ever complained that a report was too easy to read.
steps.translation: Mükemmel. Ve Deniz? Sade bir İngilizceyle yaz. Bugüne kadar kimse bir raporun fazla kolay okunduğundan şikâyet etmedi.

steps.prompt: Bu konuşma esas olarak ne hakkında?
choices: Yönetim kurulu için hazırlanacak raporun içeriği ve yapısı
steps.answer: Yönetim kurulu için hazırlanacak raporun içeriği ve yapısı

Report: Small vans for city deliveries

Introduction
This report presents the results of a six-month study on delivery vans in Istanbul. Its aim is to decide whether small vans should replace some of our trucks.

Method
We tracked 200 deliveries in Kadıköy and Beşiktaş. Half were made with trucks and half with small vans.

Findings
The results were clear. Fuel use fell by 21 per cent, and the cost per delivery dropped from 90 to 74 lira. Customers were also more satisfied, as the vans could park closer to their doors. However, the vans were not suitable for heavy orders, and drivers needed about two weeks to learn the new routes.

Limitations
The study only covered two districts, so the results may be different in other parts of the city.

Recommendations
Based on these findings, we recommend the following:
1. Replace ten old trucks with small vans next year.
2. Test the vans in two more districts before making further changes.
3. Keep two trucks for heavy orders.

Conclusion
On the whole, the evidence suggests that small vans are cheaper and greener. A gradual change is the safest option.

units.guide:
## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- Doğal hızdaki iki kişilik bir tartışmayı izleyip her konuşmacının tutumunu ayırt edebilirsin.
- Bir tartışma özetinde kimin neyi savunduğunu ve yazarın kendi görüşünü bulabilirsin.
- Bir tartışmada görüşünü söyleyip karşı görüşün haklı yanını kabul ederek cevap verebilirsin.
- İki konuşmacının görüşünü 150 kelimelik tarafsız bir özet olarak yazabilirsin.

## Strateji
- Tutumu ele veren ifadeleri dinle: katılma (**I couldn't agree more**, **fair point**), kısmi kabul (**I'll give you that**, **admittedly**), itiraz (**I'm not convinced**, **come on**).
- **but**, **though**, **mind you** sonrasına dikkat et: konuşmacının asıl görüşü çoğu zaman bu kelimelerden sonra gelir.
- Gölgeleme (shadowing): hızlı cümleleri önce 0,85 hızda, sonra normal hızda tekrarla; **I'd**, **you're**, **want to** gibi bağlantılı sesleri taklit et.
- Hikâyeyi önce metni görmeden dinle. Her konuşmacı için bir cümlelik not al (Kerem: …, Mia: …), sonra soruları cevapla ve metni açıp kontrol et.
- Özet yazarken kendi görüşünü katma; **argued**, **claimed**, **pointed out**, **stressed** gibi aktarma fiilleri kullan.

## Model metin
> In this episode of City Talk, the host Mia and Kerem, a software engineer, discussed whether remote work is good for cities.
>
> Kerem argued that remote work is mostly positive. In his view, working from home reduces traffic and pollution. He also claimed that the money people used to spend near offices has not disappeared; it is now spent in their own neighbourhoods. He believes that the real problem is management, because managers who measure results instead of hours have no reason not to trust their staff.
>
> Mia, on the other hand, was more cautious. She pointed out that many cafés in business districts have closed. She was also worried that young employees learn less when they cannot watch experienced colleagues.
>
> Interestingly, both speakers agreed that the traditional nine-to-five model is dying. However, while Kerem emphasised flexibility, Mia stressed that some people still need a desk next to someone.

Yapı: girişte konu ve konuşmacılar, her konuşmacıya bir paragraf, sonra anlaştıkları ve ayrıldıkları nokta. Aktarma fiilleri (argued, claimed, pointed out) ve karşıtlık bağlaçları (on the other hand, while) özetin omurgası.

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ It depends from the job. ✅ It depends **on** the job. (Türkçedeki "-e bağlı" İngilizcede **depend on**.)
- ❌ Mia is agree with Kerem. ✅ Mia **agrees** with Kerem. (**agree** bir fiil; önüne **is** gelmez.)

City Talk, Episode 14: Should the centre be car-free?
Summary by Mia, host

This week's episode was one of our liveliest so far. My two guests, urban planner Aylin Kaya and bookshop owner Murat Demir, disagreed on almost everything, yet they managed to stay friendly throughout.

Aylin believes that cars should be banned from the historic centre within five years. In her view, the streets were never designed for heavy traffic, and pedestrians, cyclists and buses should come first. She pointed to cities such as Ghent and Pontevedra, where car-free centres have led to cleaner air and, according to her, more visitors for local shops. "Once people can walk safely," she argued, "they stay longer and spend more."

Murat was far from convinced. He accepts that the air quality is poor, but he is worried about older customers and about deliveries. "Half of my regular customers are over sixty," he said. "If they can't park nearby, they'll simply order online." He also questioned whether examples from small European towns can be applied to a district of half a million people. What he would support is a gradual approach: car-free Sundays first, then a car-free zone around the market, and only later a full ban, depending on the results.

Interestingly, the two guests agreed on more than they expected. Both want better buses, and both think that delivery vans should be allowed in the early morning. The real disagreement was about speed. Aylin sees delay as the main risk, while Murat fears that a sudden ban would hurt small businesses before they could adapt.

Listeners were divided too. In our online poll, 54 per cent supported a full ban, 38 per cent preferred Murat's step-by-step plan and the rest were undecided.

Personally, I left the studio thinking that both of them were partly right. The goal seems clear; the timing is the hard part. Perhaps the most useful result of the discussion is that it moved the debate away from "cars or no cars" and towards "how fast, and with what support for the people most affected".

Next week: Is remote work good for cities? Kerem, a software engineer, joins me in the studio.

nodes.title: Ofis mi, ev mi?
nodes.description: Mia'nın podcastinde Kerem'le uzaktan çalışmanın şehirlere etkisini tartışıyorlar

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Welcome back to City Talk. I'm Mia, and today I'm joined by Kerem, a software engineer who hasn't been to an office for, what, three years?
steps.translation: City Talk'a tekrar hoş geldiniz. Ben Mia, bugün yanımda üç yıldır, değil mi, ofise adım atmamış bir yazılım mühendisi var: Kerem.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: Three and a half, actually. And honestly, I don't miss it at all.
steps.translation: Aslında üç buçuk. Açıkçası hiç de özlemiyorum.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Well, that's where we disagree, so let's get straight into it. Is remote work good for cities?
steps.translation: İşte orada ayrılıyoruz, o yüzden hemen konuya girelim. Uzaktan çalışma şehirler için iyi mi?

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: For people, definitely. For cities, I'd say mostly yes. Think about traffic. If a million people stay at home two days a week, the roads are emptier and the air is cleaner.
steps.translation: İnsanlar için kesinlikle. Şehirler için de bence çoğunlukla evet. Trafiği düşün. Bir milyon kişi haftada iki gün evde kalırsa yollar boşalır, hava temizlenir.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Sure, but look at the business districts. Half the cafés around the big office towers in Levent have closed. Who's going to pay those people's wages?
steps.translation: Tamam, ama iş merkezlerine bak. Levent'teki büyük ofis kulelerinin çevresindeki kafelerin yarısı kapandı. O insanların maaşını kim ödeyecek?

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: OK, that's a fair point. But the money hasn't disappeared. People are spending it in their own neighbourhoods instead. Elif's café in Moda is full of laptops every afternoon.
steps.translation: Tamam, haklı bir nokta. Ama para yok olmadı. İnsanlar onu artık kendi mahallelerinde harcıyor. Elif'in Moda'daki kafesi her öğleden sonra dizüstü bilgisayarlarla dolu.

steps.prompt: Kerem'e göre insanlar paralarını artık nerede harcıyor?

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: I'm not sure that's the whole picture. What worries me more is young people. When I started at the magazine, I learnt everything by listening to the older journalists around me.
steps.translation: Bunun tablonun tamamı olduğundan emin değilim. Beni daha çok endişelendiren gençler. Dergide başladığımda her şeyi çevremdeki deneyimli gazetecileri dinleyerek öğrendim.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: You can learn online too. Our junior developers have a video call with a mentor every day.
steps.translation: İnternetten de öğrenebilirsin. Bizim genç yazılımcılarımız her gün bir mentorla görüntülü görüşme yapıyor.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Every day? Come on. A video call isn't the same as overhearing how an editor talks to an angry writer.
steps.translation: Her gün mü? Hadi ama. Görüntülü görüşme, bir editörün kızgın bir yazarla nasıl konuştuğuna kulak misafiri olmakla aynı şey değil.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: Fine, I'll give you that. Some things are easier to learn in a room. But that's an argument for meeting sometimes, not for commuting five days a week.
steps.translation: Peki, orada haklısın. Bazı şeyleri aynı odada öğrenmek daha kolay. Ama bu ara sıra buluşmak için bir gerekçe, haftada beş gün işe gidip gelmek için değil.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: So what would you suggest? Because, to be honest, a lot of managers simply don't trust people they can't see.
steps.translation: Peki ne önerirsin? Çünkü açıkçası pek çok yönetici göremediği insanlara güvenmiyor.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: That's a management problem, not a remote work problem. If you measure results instead of hours, trust isn't an issue.
steps.translation: Bu bir yönetim sorunu, uzaktan çalışma sorunu değil. Saatleri değil sonuçları ölçersen güven sorun olmaz.

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Easier said than done. Mind you, I do agree that the old nine-to-five model is dying.
steps.translation: Söylemesi kolay. Gerçi eski dokuzdan beşe modelinin ölmekte olduğuna ben de katılıyorum.

steps.speaker: Kerem
steps.text: There you go. We agree on something!
steps.translation: İşte bak. Bir konuda anlaşıyoruz!

steps.speaker: Mia
steps.text: Let me push you a bit, though. Isn't there a risk that cities become lonelier? Lots of people make their friends at work.
steps.translation: Yine de seni biraz zorlayayım. Şehirlerin daha yalnız yerler hâline gelme riski yok mu? Pek çok insan arkadaşlarını işte ediniyor.

exercises.model:
In this episode of City Talk, the host Mia and Kerem, a software engineer, discussed whether remote work is good for cities.

Kerem argued that remote work is mostly positive. In his view, working from home reduces traffic and pollution. He also claimed that the money people used to spend near offices has not disappeared; it is now spent in their own neighbourhoods. He believes that the real problem is management, because managers who measure results instead of hours have no reason not to trust their staff.

Mia, on the other hand, was more cautious. She pointed out that many cafés in business districts have closed. She was also worried that young employees learn less when they cannot watch experienced colleagues.

Interestingly, both speakers agreed that the traditional nine-to-five model is dying. However, while Kerem emphasised flexibility, Mia stressed that some people still need a desk next to someone.

units.description: İş mülakatında kendini ayrıntılı ve esnek biçimde anlat, ön yazı yaz
units.guide:
## Bu ünitede yapabileceklerin
- İş mülakatında deneyimini, başarılarını ve hedeflerini ayrıntılı anlatabilirsin.
- Beklenmedik ya da zor sorulara esnek ve kibar cevap verebilirsin.
- Ayrıntılı bir iş ilanından görevleri, şartları ve şirketin beklentilerini bulabilirsin.
- Bir iş ilanına 200 kelimelik resmî bir ön yazı (cover letter) yazabilirsin.

## Strateji
- "Tell me about yourself" cevabını dört parçaya böl: şimdiki görevin, deneyimin (ne zamandır), gurur duyduğun bir sonuç, neden bu iş.
- Başarıyı rakamla anlat ve vurgulu yapı kullan: **What I am most proud of is…**, **It was… that…**
- Zor soruda zaman kazan: **That's a great question.** ya da **Let me think about that for a second.** Sonra kısa bir örnek ver.
- Gölgeleme (shadowing) ile mülakat cümlelerini akıcı hâle getir; hikâyeyi önce metni görmeden dinle, görüşmecinin sorularını not al, sonra metinle kontrol et.
- Ön yazıda ilandaki şartlara tek tek cevap ver ve resmî kapanış kullan: **Dear Mr…** ile başladıysan **Yours sincerely**.

## Model metin
> Dear Mr Clarke,
>
> I am writing to apply for the position of Head of Urban Logistics in Istanbul, which was advertised on your website.
>
> I have worked in logistics for six years, and for the last four years I have been an operations manager at a delivery company in Istanbul. In this role, I am responsible for a team of fourteen people and plan around three thousand deliveries a week.
>
> What I am most proud of is a six-month study on small vans. It showed that they reduced fuel use by 21 per cent and cut the cost per delivery by about a sixth. As a result, the board has approved ten new vans for next year.
>
> It is the chance to build a new team from the very beginning that attracts me most to this role. I believe that my experience with sustainable transport and my calm approach to problems would be valuable to Clarke & Vos.
>
> I have attached my CV, and I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application in more detail.
>
> Yours sincerely,
> Deniz

Yapı: başvurulan pozisyon, deneyim ve şimdiki görev, rakamlı bir başarı, bu işi neden istediğin (vurgulu **It is… that…**), kapanış ve ek. Kısaltma yok; her paragraf tek bir fikir taşıyor.

## Türklerin sık hatası
- ❌ I am working here since four years. ✅ I **have been working** here **for** four years. (Süren durum: present perfect; süre **for**, başlangıç **since**.)
- ❌ I am responsible from the budget. / I am operations manager. ✅ I am responsible **for** the budget. / I am **an** operations manager.

## Beceri testi
Bölüm 8 beceri testi 20 sorudur; geçmek için %80 doğru yap. Bölüm, bu test **ve** bu ünitenin yazma görevi (Yazma: Ön yazı) birlikte tamamlandığında bitmiş sayılır.

| Bölüm | Soru | Ölçtüğü hedef |
|---|---|---|
| Dinleme | 6 | Rapor rakamları (s8u11), tutum ve itiraz (s8u12), mülakat soruları (s8u13), söylem belirteçleri ve temkinli dil (s8u1, s8u7) |
| Okuma | 8 | Anket özeti ve temkinli sonuç (s8u11, s8u7); tavsiye yazısında yazarın tutumu ve mülakat stratejisi (s8u12, s8u13) |
| Yazma | 4 | Rapor cümlesi (s8u11), vurgulu yapı (s8u3), resmî öneri (s8u6, s8u9), deneyim ve süre (s8u13) |
| Dil | 2 | Cleft sentence (s8u3), hedging (s8u7) |

Head of Urban Logistics, Istanbul
Clarke & Vos Logistics

About us
Clarke & Vos is a family-owned logistics company based in Rotterdam. For over forty years, we have moved goods between Europe and Turkey. Next spring, we are opening our first office in Istanbul, and we are looking for someone to lead it.

The role
This is not a desk job. The Head of Urban Logistics will build a team of around 25 people from scratch and design a delivery network for both sides of the city. In the first year, you will:
- choose and manage a fleet of about 40 small electric vans;
- negotiate with local suppliers and warehouse owners;
- reduce our delivery emissions in the city by at least 30 per cent by 2028;
- report directly to the managing director in Rotterdam.

What we are looking for
- At least five years' experience in logistics, including two years managing people.
- A proven interest in sustainable transport. Experience with electric vehicles is an advantage but not essential.
- Fluent Turkish and excellent English. Dutch is not required.
- The ability to stay calm when things go wrong, because they sometimes will.

To be honest, we care less about where you studied than about what you have achieved. If you have run a project that changed the way your company works, tell us about it.

What we offer
- A competitive salary and an annual bonus linked to the team's results.
- Flexible working: two days a week from home once the office is running.
- A two-week training period at our headquarters in Rotterdam.
- The chance to shape a new office from the very beginning.

How to apply
Send your CV and a cover letter of no more than one page through the careers page of our website by 15 January. In your letter, please explain why you are interested in the role and describe one result you are particularly proud of. Interviews will take place by video call in late January. We will only contact candidates who are invited to an interview.

steps.speaker: Tom Clarke
steps.text: I watched your conference talk online. What made you start the van study?
steps.translation: Konferans konuşmanızı internetten izledim. Kamyonet çalışmasına sizi ne başlattı?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Frustration, mostly. Our trucks were spending more time in traffic than on the road. What I wanted to find out was whether smaller vehicles could solve that.
steps.translation: Çoğunlukla bıkkınlık. Kamyonlarımız yolda olduğundan çok trafikte vakit geçiriyordu. Öğrenmek istediğim şey, daha küçük araçların bunu çözüp çözemeyeceğiydi.

steps.speaker: Tom Clarke
steps.text: And the results?
steps.translation: Peki sonuçlar?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Fuel use fell by twenty-one per cent, and the cost per delivery dropped by about a sixth. The board has just approved ten new vans for next year.
steps.translation: Yakıt kullanımı yüzde yirmi bir düştü, teslimat başına maliyet de yaklaşık altıda bir azaldı. Yönetim kurulu gelecek yıl için on yeni kamyoneti az önce onayladı.

steps.speaker: Tom Clarke
steps.text: Impressive. Now, a harder question. Tell me about a time when something went badly wrong.
steps.translation: Etkileyici. Şimdi daha zor bir soru. Bir şeyin çok kötü gittiği bir zamandan bahsedin.

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: In the first month of the study, two drivers refused to use the new routes. They thought the vans were a way to cut their jobs.
steps.translation: Çalışmanın ilk ayında iki sürücü yeni rotaları kullanmayı reddetti. Kamyonetlerin işlerini ellerinden almanın bir yolu olduğunu düşünüyorlardı.

steps.speaker: Tom Clarke
steps.text: How did you handle it?
steps.translation: Bununla nasıl başa çıktınız?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: I didn't push. I sat in the van with them for a whole day and listened. It turned out that their real worry was the heavy orders. Once we kept two trucks for those, they became the study's biggest supporters.
steps.translation: Zorlamadım. Bütün bir gün onlarla kamyonette oturdum ve dinledim. Asıl endişelerinin ağır siparişler olduğu ortaya çıktı. Onlar için iki kamyon tutunca çalışmanın en büyük destekçileri oldular.

steps.prompt: "Once we kept two trucks for those" cümlesindeki 'those' neyi anlatıyor?
Bu olay Deniz hakkında ne gösteriyor?

steps.speaker: Tom Clarke
steps.text: That's exactly the kind of answer I was hoping for. Our advert asks for two years of managing people. You have more than that, I assume?
steps.translation: Tam da umduğum türden bir cevap. İlanımız iki yıllık yöneticilik deneyimi istiyor. Sizde bundan fazlası var, sanırım?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Four years. And to be completely honest, managing people is the part I find most rewarding, even on difficult days.
steps.translation: Dört yıl. Açık konuşmak gerekirse, zor günlerde bile insan yönetmek işin en tatmin edici bulduğum kısmı.

steps.speaker: Tom Clarke
steps.text: One last question. Why do you want to leave a company where you're clearly doing well?
steps.translation: Son bir soru. Belli ki başarılı olduğunuz bir şirketten neden ayrılmak istiyorsunuz?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: I'm not unhappy there. But building a new office from the very beginning is a chance I may never get again. And I'd love to show that green delivery works across the whole city, not just in two districts.
steps.translation: Orada mutsuz değilim. Ama sıfırdan yeni bir ofis kurmak bir daha belki hiç yakalayamayacağım bir fırsat. Ayrıca yeşil teslimatın sadece iki ilçede değil, bütün şehirde işe yaradığını göstermeyi çok isterim.

steps.speaker: Tom Clarke
steps.text: Thank you, Deniz. We'll let you know by Friday. Any questions for me?
steps.translation: Teşekkürler Deniz. Cumaya kadar size haber vereceğiz. Bana sormak istediğiniz bir şey var mı?

steps.prompt: Tom Clarke kararı ne zamana kadar bildirecek?

steps.speaker: Deniz
steps.text: Just one. What would success look like for this person after the first year?
steps.translation: Sadece bir tane. İlk yılın sonunda bu görevdeki kişi için başarı ne anlama gelir?

steps.speaker: Tom Clarke
steps.text: Good question. A team that trusts each other, and vans that are full, not stuck in traffic.
steps.translation: İyi soru. Birbirine güvenen bir ekip ve trafikte sıkışıp kalmayan, dolu kamyonetler.

Dear Mr Clarke,

I am writing to apply for the position of Head of Urban Logistics in Istanbul, which was advertised on your website.

I have worked in logistics for six years, and for the last four years I have been an operations manager at a delivery company in Istanbul. In this role, I am responsible for a team of fourteen people and plan around three thousand deliveries a week.

What I am most proud of is a six-month study on small vans. It showed that they reduced fuel use by 21 per cent and cut the cost per delivery by about a sixth. As a result, the board has approved ten new vans for next year.

It is the chance to build a new team from the very beginning that attracts me most to this role. I believe that my experience with sustainable transport and my calm approach to problems would be valuable to Clarke & Vos.

I have attached my CV, and I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application in more detail.

Yours sincerely,
Deniz

Summary: Laptops in local cafés
In March, a group of students surveyed 300 customers and 20 café owners in Kadıköy about people who work on laptops in cafés.
The results were mixed. Around 60 per cent of customers said they sometimes work in cafés, mostly in the afternoon. Owners, however, were divided. Eleven of the twenty said that laptop users were good for business, because they bring a steady flow of customers on quiet weekdays. The other nine complained that many of them buy one coffee and stay for three hours, which means fewer free tables at busy times.
Several owners have already found a compromise. Some offer laptop-free tables at lunchtime, while others ask customers who stay longer than two hours to order again. Interestingly, very few customers seemed to mind these rules; in fact, 72 per cent said they would accept them.
It would be wrong to draw strong conclusions from a survey of this size. Nevertheless, the findings suggest that clear and friendly rules may be the best way to keep both groups happy.

Ask Mia: "Why do you want to leave?"
Dear Mia, I have a job interview next week. I am happy in my current job, but this new position is a big step up. I am worried that they will ask why I want to leave. What should I say? Burcu
Dear Burcu, this question worries almost everyone, but it is actually a gift. What the interviewer really wants to know is not why you are leaving, but why you are coming. So talk about the new role, not the old one.
Never criticise your current employer, even if you have good reasons. It rarely sounds professional, and interviewers tend to wonder what you might one day say about them. Instead, explain what the new job offers that your current one cannot: more responsibility, a new market, a chance to build something.
It is also perfectly fine to admit that you like your present job. In fact, it can work in your favour. Candidates who are not desperate to escape often seem more confident.
Finally, prepare a short, honest answer and practise it out loud. Two or three sentences are enough. Good luck! Mia
